narrative:
Over the past 27 years, the Philadelphia City Council has churned out an astonishing 8,531 bills, a remarkable volume of legislative activity that reflects the city's relentless pursuit of progress. From zoning regulations to transportation infrastructure, this flood of legislation has shaped the very fabric of our city, with many bills ultimately making it into law: a staggering 6,593 – or nearly 99% – have been signed by mayoral signature or veto-proof majorities since 2000. This is no small feat, especially considering that over 1,800 bills remain active to this day.

A closer look at the data reveals some fascinating patterns. For instance, zoning and planning issues have dominated the Council's agenda for nearly three decades, accounting for a combined total of over 4,500 bills – more than half of all legislation introduced since 2000. Meanwhile, the number of bills introduced has ebbed and flowed over time, with some years seeing as few as 66 new introductions (in 2026) and others, like 2012 and 2018, witnessing nearly 400 new proposals each year. Perhaps most strikingly, the Council's bills have an unusually high pass rate: 99% of closed bills become law, suggesting a remarkable degree of collaboration between members.

So what can we learn from all this data? For one thing, it underscores the importance of keeping tabs on our elected representatives – tracking legislation is essential to holding them accountable for their actions. At Open Common Ground, we believe that informed citizens are empowered citizens, and our platform makes it easier than ever to stay up-to-date on Council business. By exploring these numbers and trends, Philadelphians can better understand the issues that affect their lives, connect with like-minded neighbors, and even influence policy decisions in meaningful ways – making Open Common Ground your go-to resource for navigating the City Council's legislative landscape.
